limitations: The gate binds its engine and prover as operator_asserted_not_attested executables: the record shows which bytes ran, not that they were built from the pinned sources.
Times, memory and proof sizes in gate/gate.json and the bundles are measurements of the recording host.
Gate outputs are retained as the gate wrote them and name the recording host's temporary and checkout locations as identity metadata; run.json and manifest.json hold no host path.
Digests are unkeyed: they detect accidental edits, not who produced the record. Nothing here re-runs the prover or the verifier.
note: Retained proved-heat gate records are verified for integrity only: every retained file matches the manifest and no unrecorded file is present, the gate passed with its required native tests, its SCR and SP1 revisions and trees, guest recipe, guest ELF and compiler archive are the pins CIW declares, and the retained bundles, replay receipt and re-verification report pass CIW's offline proved-heat validation. No proof is re-verified and nothing is re-executed; the digests are unkeyed.
notes: This description was written after the run from the step logs, the gate outputs and the host: the driver then in use, an earlier form of scripts/run_proved_heat_locally.py, wrote none, so driver_sha256 is null and git is not recorded.

The CIW commit is the one the checkout's reflog names as HEAD while the gate ran; uncommitted changes are not recorded. The installed wheel's digest is in gate/gate.json. src/ciw/proved_heat.py, tests/test_proved_heat.py, tests/test_proved_heat_session.py, scripts/check_proved_heat.py and the workflow are the same at that commit as at the commit that retained this record.
Step durations are whole seconds as the driver printed them.
